source.sourcePlan: Bing + Wikipedia in parallel, then Wolfram Alpha; Bing is selected first when multiple answers are available
source.sourceAttribution: Bing and Wolfram Alpha are inserted after final-period normalization; Wikipedia is not inserted

controls.name: selected HTTP success
controls.observed: Bing answer over /answer_skill/v1/main; status 200; text/html response; source JCP SLIM/PLAY; Bing timing and facts analytics

controls.name: provider priority and fallback
controls.observed: Bing wins against simultaneous Wikipedia; Wikipedia wins after Bing empty; Wolfram starts only after both first-group peers return empty

controls.name: late priority
controls.observed: Bing completing after the first-group deadline but before delayed Wolfram remains the selected answer

controls.name: all-empty and upstream errors
controls.observed: Both produce source no-answer prompt GQA_no_answer_what_01 plus DISPLAY/MIM_VIEW JSON, success:false analytics, and no provider error text

controls.name: account and attribution
controls.observed: Account HTTP lookup precedes provider calls; Bing and Wolfram records preserve normalized answer, URL, image/null, loop ID and timestamp; retrieveAtt and wipeID operate over HTTP

controls.name: status/media and route boundaries
controls.observed: Success/retrieve/wipe use 200 text/html; missing transID uses 400 text/html; missing path uses 404 ERROR JSON

controls.name: fail-closed configuration
controls.observed: Missing Wolfram or Bing endpoint throws during profile/start construction before a listener is opened

falsifiers: Letting Wikipedia answer before a ready Bing answer fails the priority assertion.
Starting Wolfram while Bing or Wikipedia has a useful first-group answer fails request-count assertions.
Settling before the late Bing response fails the late-priority answer assertion.
Replacing source no-answer MIM/display with a generic placeholder fails prompt, display, analytics and error-leak assertions.
Skipping account lookup, omitting the final period before insertion, attributing Wikipedia, or losing the Wolfram URL/image-null shape fails the account/attribution receipt.
Returning JSON media, a generic error status, or exposing an unregistered answer path fails the HTTP boundary assertions.
Using an implicit provider URL fails the missing-endpoint construction assertion.
limitations: This is a controlled current-main replay with fake peers; it does not claim live Bing, Wikipedia, Wolfram, Account, Mongo, deployment, or robot reachability.
The explicit memory attribution store is used for deterministic HTTP retrieve/wipe coverage; Mongo driver behavior remains covered by the adjacent adapter tests.
The replay covers the existing answer path only and does not exercise news implementation files.
